subject.title: fix(ai): record token usage on Responses early-abort (#100954)

question: After the PR is narrowed so it no longer claims to fix client cancellation or first-byte timeout, should exact-event processor tests be accepted as sufficient proof for the server-generated `response.incomplete` accounting fix?
rationale: The code and tests support the narrower server-terminal behavior, but only a maintainer can approve an exception to the external-PR real-behavior proof gate when the contributor lacks provider access.

options.title: Require narrow scope and live proof
options.body: Keep the linked issue open, correct the PR scope, and require a redacted OpenAI or Azure `max_output_tokens` run showing populated usage and cost.

options.title: Approve a narrow proof override
options.body: Keep the linked issue open, correct the PR scope, and explicitly accept the upstream SDK contract plus both exact-event processor regressions instead of a live provider run.

options.title: Pause pending provider access
options.body: Leave the PR open until someone with an OpenAI or Azure deployment can capture the requested runtime evidence.

recommendation.title: Require narrow scope and live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the linked issue open, correct the PR scope, and require a redacted OpenAI or Azure `max_output_tokens` run showing populated usage and cost.
